The '''2014–15 Scottish Premiership''' was the second season of the [[Scottish Premiership]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]]. The season began on 9 August 2014<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/celtic/266263-scottish-premiership-201415-campaign-set-for-start-on-august-9th/ | title=Scottish Premiership 2014/15 campaign set for start on August 9 | publisher=STV | date=6 March 2014 | access-date=6 March 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407065202/http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/celtic/266263-scottish-premiership-201415-campaign-set-for-start-on-august-9th/ | archive-date=7 April 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref> and ended on the 31 May 2015. Celtic were the defending champions.

Twelve teams contested the league: [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]], [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]], [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]], [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]], [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness CT]], [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]], [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]], [[Partick Thistle F.C.|Partick Thistle]], [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]], [[St Johnstone F.C.|St Johnstone]] and [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]. Due to the relegation of [[Edinburgh]]-based teams [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] [[2013–14 Scottish Premiership|in 2014]], this season marked the first time in football history in which a capital city had no representatives in the top league.

On 2 May, Celtic clinched their fourth title in a row after Aberdeen lost 1–0 away at Dundee United, leaving Celtic 11 points clear with three games to play.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://spfl.co.uk/news/article/celtic-retain-premiership-title/|title=Celtic retain Premiership title|publisher=SPFL|date=2 May 2015|access-date=2 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/32566809|title=Celtic win Scottish Premiership title after Aberdeen lose|date=2 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|access-date=15 May 2015}}</ref>

==Teams==
[[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]] were promoted from the [[2013–14 Scottish Championship|Scottish Championship]]. [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] were relegated from the [[2013–14 Scottish Premiership|Scottish Premiership]].

[[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] finished in the play-off position in the [[2013–14 Scottish Premiership|Scottish Premiership]]. They lost to [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] who took the final place in the second edition of the competition, a result which left the Scottish capital [[Edinburgh]] without a club in the top flight of Scottish football for the 2014–15 season.

== Tournament format and regulations ==

=== Basic ===
In the initial phase of the season, the 12 teams played a round-robin tournament whereby each team played each one of the other teams three times. After 33 games, the league split into two sections of six teams, with each team playing each other in that section. The league attempts to balance the fixture list so that teams in the same section play each other twice at home and twice away, but sometimes this is impossible. A total of 228 matches were played, with 38 matches played by each team.

=== Promotion and relegation ===
The team that finished 12th (St Mirren) was relegated to the [[Scottish Championship|Championship]], while the champion of that league (Heart of Midlothian) was promoted to the Premiership for the 2015–16 season. The team that finished 11th in the Premiership (Motherwell) played the winner of the Championship playoffs (Rangers) in two playoff games, with the winner (Motherwell) securing a Premiership spot for the 2015–16 season.
